proposed_from.topic: Graph-budget sharp counterfactual envelopes under bounded failures of context-independent inverse transport. Fix a finite-horizon shared-order scalar triangular SCM on a finite parent-context grid, mutually independent uniform ranks, rational continuous strictly increasing piecewise-affine conditional quantiles, rational-box factual evidence, and bounded rational piecewise-polynomial payoff. Put an orientation gate on every reachable mechanism-context cell; connect grid-neighbor cells in H and impose TV_H(s)≤K. Characterize attained sharp endpoint hulls for the conditional intervention payoff, zero-budget point recovery, nesting, exact Boolean-polynomial/polyhedral-integration computation with complexity or hardness bounds, and simultaneous DKW-projection inference. Report the smallest K changing each DoFlow or CausalSim decision without claiming K is identified. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Common factual ranks reduce each counterfactual reflection to products of factual and rollout orientation gates. Integrating the rational piecewise model gives an orientation-independent Boolean polynomial of degree at most twice the number of nonintervened mechanisms; an augmented factor graph then supports budgeted tree-decomposition optimization. Exact checks recovered the two-context sign-flip envelope and four-cell path endpoint pairs (-1/5,-1/5), (-1/5,2/5), (-3/10,2/5), and (-3/10,1/2) for K=0,1,2,3. Destructive checks covered disconnected graphs, non-strict nesting, changing downstream contexts, cycles, vacuous unconditional queries, ineffective encodings, zero cells, and small evidence probabilities; no matching literature collision surfaced. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove a terminating certified DKW outer-projection algorithm that preserves shared quantile reuse, changing context cells, payoff discontinuities, and the conditioning denominator, and contracts pointwise to the sharp endpoints. EARLY KILL TEST: Compare enumeration, polynomial compilation, and shrinking DKW enclosures on the four-cell witness and a two-stage rational example with a context switch and threshold payoff; excluded exact values or persistent noncontraction require pivot or stop. proposed_from.novelty_justification: The published identification frontier already includes context-independent inverse transport and exogenous isomorphism (Tan, Chen, and Du, 2026; Chen and Du, 2025), selected bijective-generation identification (Nasr-Esfahany, Alizadeh, and Shah, 2023), scalar monotone-generation identification together with nonidentifiability absent sufficient restrictions (Nasr-Esfahany and Kiciman, 2023), and monotone c-GNF equivalence (Sourabh Balgi, Peña, and Daoud, 2024). The proposal does not claim novelty for those complete-agreement components, and the zero-budget equality is solely the known sanity corollary of Tan, Chen, and Du (2026, Theorem 2). Published partial-identification objects include curvature sensitivity for continuous counterfactuals (Melnychuk, Frauen, and Feuerriegel, 2023) and latent-law neighborhoods (Christensen and Connault, 2023); no formal containment relation with the graph-budget class is claimed. Published computational methods include finite-discrete polynomial bounding (Duarte et al., 2024), exact and approximate discrete credal-network bounding (Zaffalon et al., 2024), generic marginal-MAP machinery (Liu and Ihler, 2013), and generic signed-hypergraph optimization (Del Pia and Khajavirad, 2024), so generic counterfactual-bound optimization is not a novelty claim. Conditional on declared exact rational SCM or surrogate membership, the residual advance begins with primitive local continuous bijections having fixed cell pushforwards, derives their intrinsic orientation field, and budgets its graph-local failures to obtain attained conditional-payoff hulls and a continuous shared-rank Boolean compiler with attaining SCM backpointers. The explicit rational triangular witness certifies the graph-TV plateaus inside a legal SCM. Massart (1990), Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019), Christensen and Connault (2023), and Tan, Blanchet, and Syrgkanis (2024) supply empirical-process, endpoint-inference, and asymptotic-containment precursors but not the stagewise finite-sample projection or the open terminating almost-surely contracting projector for an endpoint-anchored, same-support, fully coupled alternative quantile law with reused inverse quantiles, adaptive contexts, discontinuous payoffs, and its induced conditioning denominator. Exact membership remains an auditable input condition rather than a claim about an unrestricted physical law.

seed_details.anchor: TanChenDu2026NMTS, Theorems 1--2 and Proposition 1; Massart1990DKW; KaidoMolinariStoye2019Projection, Theorems 3.1--3.2
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace context-independent inverse transport in the induction by one reused cellwise orientation field, then project one simultaneous empirical-CDF fiber rather than a selected quantile fit.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from DKW plus finite enumeration because there are finitely many signs.
seed_details.rebuttal: The nuisance quantile fiber is infinite-dimensional, repeated inverse-quantile calls cannot vary independently, rollout contexts switch, and the payoff is a discontinuous ratio; finite sign enumeration does not yield a terminating contracting projection.

seed_details.anchor: DuarteEtAl2024Autobounds, Theorem 1 and Algorithm 1; LiuIhler2013MarginalMAP, Section 2.3; DelPiaKhajavirad2024Hypergraph, Sections 3 and 5
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Compile common-rank integrals into factors before optimizing one globally shared orientation field and define width on the augmented factor graph rather than on the switch graph.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate generic pseudo-Boolean dynamic programming on a tree decomposition.
seed_details.rebuttal: Generic dynamic programming starts only after the causal semantics have been compiled without selector duplication; the new step is the exact continuous-rank factorization with adaptive contexts and attaining SCM backpointers.

seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Restrict the exogenous-isomorphism induction to factual and rollout cells touched by one query and prove necessity by decoding two legal global fields.
seed_details.red_team: The iff criterion is merely constancy of the target on its compatibility fiber.
seed_details.rebuttal: A publishable version must replace tautological fiber constancy by a graph-incidence criterion and a globally gluable pair of observationally equivalent triangular SCMs.

seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace inversion of a smooth sensitivity frontier by exact value-function comparison over nested graph-cut budgets with plateaus and ties.
seed_details.red_team: The smallest changing budget follows immediately after all endpoint programs are solved.
seed_details.rebuttal: That objection caps the seed as a standalone kernel; it survives only as a consumer-facing corollary with joint budget-state certificates.

seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace smooth finite-dimensional projection geometry by a target-restricted error bound for a finite union of fractional piecewise-polynomial orientation faces.
seed_details.red_team: Semialgebraic maps are automatically locally Holder, so the exponent is standard geometry.
seed_details.rebuttal: Existence of an exponent is not the target; necessity, computability, and matched perturbation sequences at active orientation and denominator singularities are unresolved.

seed_details.seed: Finite-knot extremal reduction for DKW fibers
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Show that extrema over all monotone quantiles inside simultaneous bands have representatives with knots drawn from a finite arrangement closed under shared factual and rollout reuse.
seed_details.red_team: Extreme points of an isotonic band are step functions, so finite reduction is routine.
seed_details.rebuttal: Strictly increasing continuous quantiles, repeated arguments, endogenous context switches, and a fractional conditional target prevent independent coordinatewise extreme-point selection.

seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Optimize which context adjacencies must be enforced so a specified query regains point identification at minimum repair cost.
seed_details.red_team: This is a minimum cut after the relevant cells are known.
seed_details.rebuttal: Adaptive rollout makes relevance orientation-dependent, but a theorem-level kernel would still need a nontrivial iff characterization beyond a repackaged cut problem.

seed_details.seed: Common-field contrast bounds for competing interventions
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Optimize the payoff difference of two interventions under one shared orientation field instead of subtracting separately optimized marginal intervals.
seed_details.red_team: Jointly bounding a contrast is an obvious change of objective in the same optimizer.
seed_details.rebuttal: The shared-field contrast can be strictly tighter, but absent a structural closed form or decision frontier it is better treated as a corollary than a separate angle.

seed_details.anchor: DelPiaKhajavirad2024Hypergraph, Theorems in Sections 3 and 4; DuarteEtAl2024Autobounds, Section 4
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Realize a hard bounded-degree signed-hypergraph family as orientation polynomials of legal connected-grid triangular SCM queries.
seed_details.rebuttal: It does not transfer until arbitrary signed factors are represented by legal shared-rank SCMs without breaking connectivity, positivity, or bounded payoff structure.

proposed_from.literature_map: The selected seed was checked against five adjacent threads. Tan, Chen, and Du (2026, Introduction, Theorems 1--2, Remark 1, Proposition 1, and Limitations) prove the all-or-nothing transport result and supply the first altered induction step. Chen and Du (2025, Introduction, Theorem 3.1, proof sketch, and Conclusion) establish exogenous isomorphism as a sufficient model-level bridge. Duarte et al. (2024, Introduction, Theorem 1, Algorithm 1, and Sections 9--10) polynomialize finite discrete causal bounds but do not compile continuous shared ranks. Christensen and Connault (2023, Introduction, Proposition 2.1, Theorem 2.1, inference section, and Conclusion) optimize latent-law neighborhoods, a different sensitivity object. Massart (1990) supplies the sharp two-sided DKW inequality; Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019, Introduction, Theorems 3.1--3.2, proof appendix, and Conclusion) project calibrated finite-dimensional moment regions. Tan, Blanchet, and Syrgkanis (2024, Introduction, Theorem 4.1, Proposition 4.2, and Conclusion) show why continuous causal partial-identification consistency requires joint approximation, sampling, and optimization control. Liu and Ihler (2013, Introduction, Section 2.3, Theorem 1, proof, and Conclusion) establish the noncommutativity warning. Del Pia and Khajavirad (2024, Introduction, Sections 3--5, and Conclusion) locate generic pseudo-Boolean width boundaries. Masten and Poirier (2020, Introduction, identification theorem, inference proof, and Conclusion) provide the breakdown-frontier writing model. Exact arXiv searches for context-independent inverse transport with bounds, orientation gates with counterfactuals, shared ranks with counterfactuals, DKW with partial identification, and treewidth with causal bounds found no closer paper; the exact orientation-gate query returned only Tan, Chen, and Du.
